question: A 61-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of a 3-hour history of pain and redness of both eyes. He has new blurry vision and difficulty opening his eyes in bright surroundings. He has not had any recent trauma. He uses contact lenses daily. He had surgery on his left eye 6 months ago after a penetrative trauma caused by a splinter. His vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows congestion of the perilimbal conjunctivae bilaterally. Visual acuity is decreased bilaterally. Ocular movements are normal. Slit-lamp examination shows a cornea with normal contours and leukocytes in the anterior chambers of both eyes. The eyelids, eyelashes, and lacrimal ducts show no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's condition?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Contact lens use daily -> increased risk of corneal infection -> possible corneal infection with Pseudomonas aeruginosa -> 70% confidence CHAIN: Surgery on left eye 6 months ago after splinter trauma -> possible complications leading to current eye symptoms -> 50% confidence CHAIN: Presence of leukocytes in anterior chambers of both eyes -> sign of inflammation or infection -> possible corneal infection with Pseudomonas aeruginosa -> 60% confidence CHAIN: Decreased visual acuity bilaterally -> suggests a bilateral eye condition -> possible systemic cause affecting both eyes -> 40% confidence CHAIN: Congestion of perilimbal conjunctivae bilaterally -> sign of ocular inflammation -> possible corneal infection with Pseudomonas aeruginosa -> 70%
analysis: The patient's presentation with pain, redness, blurry vision, and difficulty opening eyes in bright light, along with leukocytes in the anterior chambers of both eyes, is suggestive of acute anterior uveitis. This condition is commonly associated with autoimmune diseases, infections, or prior eye trauma.
